- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in recent history.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after recent high prices, then underestimates as prices correct downward.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, often by 1–3% relative to true values.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model fails to capture the full extent of the trend, underestimating peak values.
- Model is overly sensitive to recent volatility — overreacts to short-term noise, leading to erratic forecasts.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 1–2% for the last 5–10 days if recent history shows downward momentum.
- Model should be scaled down by 1–3% if the last 5 days show a clear downward trend or mean reversion signal.
- Avoid overfitting to recent spikes — reduce forecast amplitude by 10–20% if the last 3–5 days show no sustained upward momentum.
